name: Simple Analytics
tagline: Privacy-first website analytics without cookies or personal tracking

pricing.notes: Official pricing checked 2026-07-30; Starter listed at $20/month.
pricing.freeTier: Free for one user and 5 websites with 30 days of history; paid keeps data longer.

tiers.name: Free
tiers.limits: 1 user, 5 websites, 30 days of history and unlimited pageviews under fair use; badge required.

tiers.name: Simple (100k monthly data points)
tiers.limits: 100,000 monthly pageviews/data points and 1 included user; website count is not numerically capped on the plan card.
tiers.notes: Annual plan gives 2 months free; higher traffic changes the price.

tiers.name: Enterprise
tiers.limits: Custom traffic, users and service terms; numeric limits and price not public.

pricing.freeTierCaps: 1 user, 5 websites, 30-day data history and unlimited pageviews under fair use; a Simple Analytics badge is required.
pricing.billingTerms: monthly + annual (2 months free); self-serve bill automatically follows measured traffic
pricing.hiddenCosts: Paid pricing rises automatically with traffic: monthly plans use the current month then a 3-month average; annual plans can auto-increase after a 1-week warning. Each extra user costs $20/month. Bitcoin payment is annual-only and adds 10%; bank-transfer invoices of at least $500 add 10%.

verdictSummary: Pageview analytics, events, dashboards, and exports are very buildable; paid value is hosted privacy posture, reports, reliability, and support.
coreLoopDIY: Add JS tracker, record anonymous pageviews/events, aggregate by dimensions, and expose dashboard/API.
whyPeopleStillPay: They pay for low-maintenance analytics they can put in a privacy policy with confidence.

priorArt.name: Umami
priorArt.desc: Open-source web analytics platform for privacy-friendly tracking.

alternatives.name: GoatCounter
alternatives.desc: The spartan version: useful traffic numbers and very little else to argue about.

facts.install: Create a hosted account or run the single static binary or Docker image
facts.dataFormat: A self-hosted instance uses SQLite by default or PostgreSQL; the hosted service stores analytics on GoatCounter's infrastructure and supports JSON and CSV exports
facts.gapVsPaid: It is much more spartan and lacks Simple Analytics' polished reports, automations and privacy-focused workflow conveniences.
facts.setupBlocker: None for hosted use; self-hosting needs a reachable binary or container plus a public URL and TLS

alternatives.name: Plausible Community Edition
alternatives.desc: A nearly identical promise, delivered from a Compose file you own.

facts.install: Deploy the Community Edition with the official Docker Compose installer
facts.dataFormat: Account and configuration records live in PostgreSQL and analytics events live in ClickHouse on the user's server
facts.gapVsPaid: The core promise is similar, but the user operates the stack and Community Edition does not include every hosted-cloud extra.
facts.setupBlocker: Docker Compose, roughly 2 GB of RAM, a domain with DNS and TLS, and backups for PostgreSQL and ClickHouse

alternatives.name: Umami
alternatives.desc: Privacy analytics without cookies, personal profiles or a monthly invoice.

facts.install: Create an Umami Cloud account or deploy the Node application with Docker Compose and PostgreSQL
facts.dataFormat: A self-hosted deployment stores analytics and account data in PostgreSQL; Umami Cloud stores it in Umami's managed service
facts.gapVsPaid: It exposes more configuration and dashboard complexity while offering fewer of Simple Analytics' reporting conveniences.
facts.setupBlocker: None for hosted signup; self-hosting requires Docker or Node hosting and a PostgreSQL database

notes: Another strong yes; helps cluster analytics apps on the site.
prompt:
Build me privacy-first web analytics to replace Simple Analytics, self-hosted for my own
sites. Requirements:

- A Node + Express service with better-sqlite3: one /collect endpoint and a dashboard at
  /dash behind basic auth (password in .env).
- A tracker snippet under 1 KB of plain JS, no cookies: sends path, referrer, screen
  width, and a daily-salted hash of IP + user agent for unique counting; the salt
  rotates daily so nothing is traceable across days.
- Keep raw hits 30 days; a nightly node-cron job aggregates into daily rollups per site
  (pageviews, uniques, top pages, top referrers, device split), keeps rollups forever,
  deletes expired raw hits.
- Custom events via sa('signup') in the snippet, counted per day.
- Dashboard per site: a 30-day chart (hand-rolled SVG, no chart library), pages and
  referrers tables, a date-range picker.
- Filter obvious bots by user-agent list; ignore my own visits via a localStorage opt-
  out flag.
- CSV export per site and month from the dashboard.
- No cookies and no personal data stored, GDPR-sane by construction.
- Out of scope: funnels, session replay, and multi-user access. Uptime is on me; the
  collect endpoint sits behind my existing reverse proxy.
- README: the snippet to paste and the Caddy or nginx route.
